# New Physics Constraints on B_s → μ⁺μ⁻ from Meson Mixing Data

This letter presents an analysis of how recent measurements of B_s–B̄_s mixing serve to constrain possible new physics contributions to the rare decay B_s → μ⁺μ⁻. Since this decay is highly suppressed in the Standard Model and proceeds only through loop-level electroweak processes, it represents a particularly sensitive probe for physics beyond the Standard Model. Any new particles or interactions that could enhance the B_s → μ⁺μ⁻ branching ratio would need to be consistent with the full set of available experimental constraints, making a combined analysis of related processes essential for assessing the true discovery potential of this channel.

The study first addresses new physics scenarios characterized by vector and axial-vector quark couplings. It is shown that such contributions are already severely restricted by existing experimental data on the semileptonic decays B → (K, K*) μ⁺μ⁻. The differential distributions and branching ratios measured in these channels provide stringent bounds on the size of possible vector and axial-vector new physics amplitudes, leaving little room for these operators to significantly affect the B_s → μ⁺μ⁻ rate.

The central result of this work concerns new physics contributions with scalar and pseudoscalar quark couplings, which are less directly constrained by the B → K^(*) μ⁺μ⁻ data alone. To address this, the analysis exploits the correlation between B_s–B̄_s mixing and analogous processes in the kaon sector, namely K⁰–K̄⁰ mixing and the decay K_L → μ⁺μ⁻. Because scalar-pseudoscalar operators that contribute to B_s mixing and to B_s → μ⁺μ⁻ typically share a common operator structure with those relevant to kaon physics, the well-measured K⁰–K̄⁰ mixing parameters and the K_L → μ⁺μ⁻ branching ratio provide powerful, complementary constraints. By combining these kaon-sector observables with the B_s–B̄_s mixing measurements, the analysis is able to place tight bounds on the magnitude of scalar-pseudoscalar new physics contributions to B_s → μ⁺μ⁻.

Taken together, these constraints from vector/axial-vector and scalar/pseudoscalar sectors lead to the central conclusion of the letter: within the class of new physics models considered, the B_s → μ⁺μ⁻ branching ratio cannot be enhanced by more than a factor of two relative to its Standard Model prediction. This result establishes a robust and model-independent upper bound on the observable effects of new physics in this decay channel, providing an important benchmark for interpreting future precision measurements of B_s → μ⁺μ⁻ at experiments such as those at the LHC.

# Constraints on New Physics in B_s → μ⁺μ⁻ from B_s–B̄_s Mixing

## I. Introduction

The recent precise measurement of the B_s–B̄_s oscillation frequency by the CDF and D0 collaborations represents a milestone in flavor physics, providing the first direct determination of the mass difference Δm_s in the B_s meson system. This measurement, combined with theoretical predictions for the Standard Model (SM) contribution, opens a new window for constraining new physics (NP) contributions in the b→s sector. In particular, since both B_s–B̄_s mixing and the rare decay B_s → μ⁺μ⁻ are governed by similar short-distance operators, any NP model that generates observable effects in one process is generically expected to contribute to the other. This interconnection allows us to translate the precision of the mixing measurement into stringent bounds on the branching ratio of B_s → μ⁺μ⁻.

The decay B_s → μ⁺μ⁻ is helicity suppressed in the SM, leading to an extremely small predicted branching ratio, BR(B_s → μ⁺μ⁻)_SM ≈ 3.5 × 10⁻⁹. This suppression makes the channel exceptionally sensitive to new physics contributions that lift the helicity suppression, most notably scalar and pseudoscalar operators that arise naturally in extensions of the SM such as the Minimal Supersymmetric Standard Model (MSSM) at large tan β. In such scenarios, Higgs-mediated flavor-changing neutral current (FCNC) processes can generate sizable scalar-pseudoscalar (S-P) operators of the form (b̄P_Rs)(μ̄P_Lμ) and its conjugate, which contribute both to B_s → μ⁺μ⁻ and, through box- and Higgs-penguin diagrams, to B_s–B̄_s mixing itself.

The purpose of this Letter is to systematically analyze the impact of the B_s–B̄_s mixing measurement on the allowed size of these S-P operators, and consequently on the maximal enhancement of BR(B_s → μ⁺μ⁻) relative to the SM value. Since the same effective operators that mediate B_s mixing can, in specific NP scenarios, be related by SU(3)-flavor or Grand Unified symmetries to analogous operators in the K meson system, we further exploit constraints from K⁰–K̄⁰ mixing (encoded in the ε_K parameter) and from the leptonic decay K_L → μ⁺μ⁻ to sharpen our bounds. Combining these three pieces of experimental information—Δm_s, ε_K, and BR(K_L → μ⁺μ⁻)—allows us to place a essentially model-independent upper limit on the possible NP enhancement of B_s → μ⁺μ⁻.

## II. Effective Hamiltonian and Operator Basis

We work in the framework of an effective Hamiltonian valid below the electroweak scale, in which NP effects are parametrized by a set of local operators of dimension six. For B_s–B̄_s mixing, in addition to the SM operator O_VLL = (b̄_Lγ_μs_L)(b̄_Lγ^μs_L), we allow for the presence of scalar and pseudoscalar operators

O_LR = (b̄_Ls_R)(b̄_Rs_L),  O_SLL = (b̄_Ls_R)(b̄_Ls_R) + h.c.,

which arise from the exchange of neutral Higgs bosons in models with an extended Higgs sector. The Wilson coefficients of these operators, evaluated at the matching scale, depend on the specific NP model; however, their contribution to the mass difference Δm_s can be written generically as

Δm_s = Δm_s^SM [1 + κ_S C_S + κ_LR C_LR + ...],

where κ_i encode known QCD renormalization and hadronic matrix element factors (with B_s bag parameters extracted from lattice QCD), and C_i are the NP Wilson coefficients normalized to the SM one.

For the decay B_s → μ⁺μ⁻, the relevant low-energy Lagrangian contains, besides the SM axial-vector operator, the scalar and pseudoscalar four-fermion operators

O_S = (b̄P_Rs)(μ̄μ),  O_P = (b̄P_Rs)(μ̄γ_5μ),

whose Wilson coefficients C_S, C_P are generated at one loop by neutral Higgs exchange and are proportional to tan³β / M_A² in the MSSM framework, where M_A is the mass of the pseudoscalar Higgs boson. Crucially, the same combination of couplings that generates C_S, C_P also contributes to the B_s mixing amplitude through double Higgs-penguin diagrams, establishing a direct correlation between the two observables.

## III. Correlating B_s Mixing and K Meson Constraints

A key observation of this work is that in a broad class of NP models—particularly those with a universal or minimally flavor-violating structure for the Higgs-mediated FCNC couplings—the same short-distance dynamics responsible for the S-P contributions to B_s mixing also induces analogous effects in the K⁰–K̄⁰ system. The relevant K meson operators are related to those in the B_s system by the interchange of down and strange quark fields, with the overall NP coefficients scaling according to the fermion mass hierarchy and CKM factors.

Since ε_K is measured with high precision and is well described by the SM, any new S-P contribution to K⁰–K̄⁰ mixing must be highly suppressed, translating into a stringent bound on the analogous B_s-sector coupling once the flavor structure relating the two systems is specified. We supplement this with the experimental bound (or measurement) on BR(K_L → μ⁺μ⁻), which further constrains the pseudoscalar coupling to leptons—the same coupling entering the B_s → μ⁺μ⁻ amplitude.

By combining these three observables:

1. Δm_s (constraining |C_LR|, |C_S| in B_s mixing),
2. ε_K (constraining the corresponding K-sector coefficients),
3. BR(K_L → μ⁺μ⁻) (constraining the lepton coupling to the pseudoscalar operator),

we obtain a set of correlated bounds on the parameter space of the underlying NP couplings. We perform a global fit including current experimental uncertainties on Δm_s (and its SM prediction, dominated by lattice uncertainties on f_Bs√B_Bs), ε_K, and the K_L → μ⁺μ⁻ branching ratio, together with the hadronic input parameters relevant for each observable.

## IV. Results

Our numerical analysis, performed by scanning over the allowed NP parameter space consistent at the 95% confidence level with all three constraints described above, shows that the resulting bound on the S-P Wilson coefficients is significantly more restrictive than that obtained from Δm_s alone. This is primarily due to the strong suppression imposed by ε_K, which severely restricts scenarios in which large S-P couplings are present in the down-quark sector, and by the direct kinematic and helicity-structure similarity between K_L → μ⁺μ⁻ and B_s → μ⁺μ⁻, both proceeding through pseudoscalar lepton couplings.

We find that the resulting branching ratio for B_s → μ⁺μ⁻ satisfies

BR(B_s → μ⁺μ⁻) ≲ 2 × BR(B_s → μ⁺μ⁻)_SM,

at the 95% confidence level, once all three constraints are imposed simultaneously. This represents a substantial tightening compared to bounds derived from Δm_s alone, which typically allow enhancements of an order of magnitude or more. The improvement arises because the combination of K-physics observables closes a "flat direction" in parameter space that would otherwise permit large cancellations between different NP contributions to Δm_s while still allowing large S-P couplings to survive.

We emphasize that this bound, while derived under the assumption of a specific flavor-coupling relation between the B_s and K sectors (motivated by minimal flavor violation or similar symmetry principles), is rather generic among realistic NP scenarios that generate sizable Higgs-mediated FCNC effects, such as supersymmetric models at large tan β.

## V. Conclusions

We have demonstrated that the recent measurement of B_s–B̄_s mixing, when combined with existing precision data on K⁰–K̄⁰ mixing and the K_L → μ⁺μ⁻ decay rate, provides a powerful tool for constraining new physics contributions to the rare decay B_s → μ⁺μ⁻, particularly those mediated by scalar-pseudoscalar operators. Our combined analysis shows that the maximal enhancement of BR(B_s → μ⁺μ⁻) over its SM value is limited to approximately a factor of 2, a result that significantly restricts the viable parameter space for new physics models featuring large Higgs-mediated FCNC couplings, such as the MSSM at large tan β. This bound implies that an observation of BR(B_s → μ⁺μ⁻) significantly above 10⁻⁸ at the Tevatron or LHC experiments would either require additional new physics contributions beyond simple scalar-pseudoscalar Higgs exchange, or a departure from the flavor symmetry relations assumed in relating the B_s and K meson sectors. Future improvements in the determination of Δm_s from lattice QCD, together with more precise measurements of BR(K_L → μ⁺μ⁻) and continued experimental progress on B_s → μ⁺μ⁻ itself, will allow this bound to be sharpened further, providing an increasingly incisive test of new physics scenarios in the flavor sector.

# Setting a New Standard: What It Means to Start Here

Every great transformation begins with a single word: **new**. New ideas, new approaches, new possibilities. But turning "new" into something meaningful requires more than just novelty—it requires purpose and direction.

**Here** is where that journey starts. Not somewhere else, not "eventually," but right now, in this exact moment. Progress isn't a distant destination; it's built one decision at a time, starting from wherever we currently stand. Whether you're launching a project, adopting a fresh habit, or rethinking how you approach a challenge, the starting point is always "here"—the present circumstances, however imperfect they may be.

But new beginnings alone aren't enough. Without direction, they easily lose momentum or drift into inconsistency. This is where the idea of a **standard** becomes essential. A standard is not a limitation—it's a foundation. It represents the benchmark of quality, the principles that guide decisions, and the consistency that turns fleeting inspiration into lasting change.

When these three elements come together—embracing what's *new*, committing to action *here*, and holding to a clear *standard*—something powerful emerges: sustainable progress. It's the difference between chasing trends and building something that lasts.

So the next time you feel the pull toward something new, remember: the change starts here, and it's the standard you set that will determine how far it goes.

# Abstract

Recent precision measurements of $B_s$–$\bar{B}_s$ mixing provide stringent new constraints on the parameter space of physics beyond the Standard Model, with important implications for the rare decay $B_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$. In this Letter, we analyze the interplay between these two observables within a model-independent effective field theory framework, focusing on new physics contributions mediated by scalar and pseudoscalar operators. We show that the mass difference $\Delta M_s$ and the CP-violating phase $\phi_s$, now measured with improved accuracy, place tight bounds on the Wilson coefficients associated with scalar-pseudoscalar four-fermion operators that also govern the branching ratio for $B_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$. Combining these constraints with the current experimental measurement of $\mathrm{BR}(B_s \to \mu^+\mu^-)$, we derive updated limits on the parameter space of representative new physics scenarios, including two-Higgs-doublet models and supersymmetric extensions with large $\tan\beta$, where such scalar operators arise naturally. We further incorporate constraints from $K^0$–$\bar{K}^0$ mixing, which, through minimal flavor violation or partial compositeness assumptions relating the down-type quark sectors, impose additional restrictions on the same new physics couplings. We find that the combined constraints from $B_s$ mixing, $K$ mixing, and $B_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$ significantly reduce the allowed room for large new physics effects in scalar-pseudoscalar operators, pushing the associated new physics scale beyond several TeV in generic flavor scenarios. Our results demonstrate the complementarity of mixing observables and rare leptonic decays in probing the flavor structure of new physics, and highlight $B_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$ as an increasingly discriminating probe as mixing measurements continue to improve in precision at the LHCb and Belle II experiments.

# Abstract

The rare decay $B_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$ provides a powerful probe of physics beyond the Standard Model, particularly scenarios involving scalar and pseudoscalar operators that can significantly enhance its branching ratio relative to the SM prediction. In this work, we examine constraints on such scalar-pseudoscalar new physics contributions by exploiting the interplay between $B_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$ and a set of complementary flavor observables: recent precision measurements of $B_s$–$\bar{B}_s$ mixing, the well-measured $K^0$–$\bar{K}^0$ mixing parameter $\Delta M_K$ and $\epsilon_K$, and the experimentally stringent bound on $K_L \to \mu^+\mu^-$. Since scalar-pseudoscalar operators typically arise from new physics coupling to both down-type quark generations, correlations between the $B_s$ and $K$ sectors emerge naturally in a broad class of models (e.g., those with generic Yukawa-like flavor structures or minimal flavor violation extensions). We perform a combined analysis incorporating the current experimental world averages and next-to-leading-order hadronic matrix elements, translating bounds from $\Delta M_{B_s}$, $\Delta M_K$, $\epsilon_K$, and $\mathcal{B}(K_L\to\mu^+\mu^-)$ into constraints on the effective Wilson coefficients governing the scalar-pseudoscalar operators relevant for $B_s\to\mu^+\mu^-$. We find that the kaon sector observables, especially the short-distance contribution extracted from $K_L\to\mu^+\mu^-$, impose severe restrictions on the allowed parameter space, particularly in models with universal or minimally broken flavor symmetry linking the $s$–$d$ and $b$–$s$ transitions. Combining all constraints, we derive an upper bound on the possible enhancement of $\mathcal{B}(B_s\to\mu^+\mu^-)$ over its Standard Model value, finding that scalar-pseudoscalar new physics contributions can increase the branching ratio by at most a factor of $\mathcal{O}(1)$–few relative to the SM expectation, once all mixing and leptonic decay constraints are simultaneously imposed. This result significantly sharpens the discriminating power of future precision measurements of $B_s\to\mu^+\mu^-$ at LHCb and Belle II for identifying or excluding scalar-mediated new physics scenarios.

Using an effective field theory framework, we systematically analyze the operators contributing to these observables, allowing for both scalar/pseudoscalar and (axial-)vector new physics contributions. We find that the requirement of consistency with precision measurements of ΔM_s, ε_K, and the differential branching ratios and angular observables in B → K(*)μ⁺μ⁻ imposes stringent bounds on the size of new physics contributions to the Wilson coefficients relevant for B_s → μ⁺μ⁻. In particular, scalar and pseudoscalar operators—often invoked to generate large deviations in B_s → μ⁺μ⁻—are tightly constrained by their radiative contributions to B_s mixing and by their interplay with the strong bound from ε_K when embedded in realistic flavor models. Combining these constraints, we derive a model-independent upper limit on the enhancement of BR(B_s → μ⁺μ⁻) relative to its Standard Model prediction, finding that new physics can increase this branching ratio by at most a factor of two. This result provides a sharp, testable benchmark for interpreting future precision measurements of B_s → μ⁺μ⁻ at LHCb and Belle II, and highlights the complementary power of rare kaon and B-meson decay data in constraining new physics in the flavor sector.

# Abstract

The rare decay $B_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$ provides a sensitive probe of physics beyond the Standard Model, with scalar and pseudoscalar operators constituting particularly interesting sensitivity targets since they are helicity-unsuppressed and can dominate the branching ratio even for small new physics couplings. While vector and axial-vector operators contributing to $b \to s\ell^+\ell^-$ transitions have been extensively constrained through measurements of $B \to K^{(*)}\mu^+\mu^-$ branching ratios and angular observables, scalar and pseudoscalar operators can additionally contribute to $B_s$-$\bar{B}_s$ mixing at one loop, offering a complementary and largely unexploited avenue of constraint. In this work, we exploit the precisely measured $B_s$-$\bar{B}_s$ oscillation frequency $\Delta M_s$ to derive bounds on the Wilson coefficients of scalar and pseudoscalar four-fermion operators relevant to $B_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$. We compute the one-loop contribution of these operators to the mixing amplitude, accounting for renormalization group running between the new physics scale and the $b$-quark mass scale, and compare the resulting constraints to those obtained directly from the current experimental bound on $\mathcal{B}(B_s \to \mu^+\mu^-)$. We find that for generic flavor structures the $\Delta M_s$ constraint is highly competitive with, and in some regions of parameter space significantly stronger than, the direct branching ratio bound, particularly for pseudoscalar operators whose contribution to mixing is not chirally suppressed. We discuss the interplay of these constraints with existing bounds on vector and axial-vector operators from $B \to K^{(*)}\mu^+\mu^-$, and outline the implications for models of new physics—such as those with an extended Higgs sector or leptoquarks—that predict enhanced scalar or pseudoscalar contributions to $b \to s\mu^+\mu^-$ transitions. Our results demonstrate that $B_s$ mixing observables should be regarded as an essential ingredient in global fits to $b \to s\ell^+\ell^-$ data.

The rare decay $B_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$ provides a powerful probe of new physics scenarios featuring scalar and pseudoscalar operators, which can significantly enhance the branching ratio beyond its Standard Model prediction while remaining consistent with current experimental measurements due to potential cancellations or specific parameter choices. In this letter, we investigate the extent to which such scalar-pseudoscalar contributions are constrained by complementary flavor observables, namely $K^0$-$\bar{K}^0$ and $B_s$-$\bar{B}_s$ mixing, as well as the rare kaon decay $K_L \to \mu^+\mu^-$. Since scalar and pseudoscalar operators generically arise from the same class of new physics that induces $\Delta F=2$ processes and modifies leptonic kaon decays, these observables offer stringent and largely model-independent bounds on the size of the corresponding Wilson coefficients. We perform a combined analysis incorporating the current experimental precision on $K$ and $B_s$ mixing parameters together with the stringent limit on $\mathcal{B}(K_L \to \mu^+\mu^-)$, translating these constraints into an upper bound on the allowed scalar-pseudoscalar new physics contribution to $B_s \to \mu^+\mu^-$. We find that, under generic assumptions of minimal flavor violation, the branching ratio enhancement is limited to less than approximately 10% relative to the Standard Model value, thereby significantly restricting the room for new physics in this channel and sharpening the interpretation of future precision measurements at LHCb and Belle II.
